newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends lower on harvest pressure, rains.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends lower on harvest pressure, rains.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled at their lowest levels in nearly four months on active harvesting in the southern U.S. Plains and on the arrival of much-needed rainfall in North Dakota, traders said.
"There was just nothing friendly for wheat today," a KCBT trader said. "We were grinding lower in search of some level where buying might come in."

Weekend rainfall across North Dakota and forecasts for more rain over the next week should give the dark northern spring wheat crop a boost. The moisture forced MGE spring wheat futures to close sharply lower.
Meanwhile, harvesting of the HRW wheat crop advanced rapidly over the weekend in southern Oklahoma, and dealers said the wheat that was cut looked to be of good quality.
"Yields are better than expected in the freeze-damaged areas (of Oklahoma)," a KCBT trader said.
Further weakness came in the form of spillover pressure from CBOT soybeans, which ended weak on nearly ideal growing weather and renewed talk that U.S. firms were importing South American supplies.
KCBT wheat saw limited support from scale-down mill-related buying, traders said.
KCBT wheat settled 5-1/2 to nine cents per bushel lower, with July down nine cents at $3.64.
Cargill Investor Services was a featured player, selling 3.4 million July bushels and 1.5 million September. Linnco Futures Group sold 1.3 million July, traders said.
Wolcott Lincoln bought two million September and bought 1.0 million bushels of the Sept/Dec spread.
